title: Rethinking Africa’s green mineral future: foreign direct investment or foreign direct constraints
body:
Africa has so far missed the transformative potential of foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows into its resource sector.

In fact, the prevailing model of FDI has not helped to overcome the resource curse; in many cases, it has actively reproduced it.

It is no longer news that Africa is richly endowed with mineral resources capable of unlocking much-needed industrialization. Yet most foreign investment continues to bypass the industries that could fundamentally transform African economies.

The result is a persistent pattern: FDI flows overwhelmingly into extraction—mining raw materials—while processing, manufacturing, and local value addition remain largely neglected as can be observed in the figure.

The resulting challenge is somewhat related to my earlier argument about financing Africa’s industrialization (see Policy Insights N10 [https://lnkd.in/eyZB2mZE] and N8 [https://lnkd.in/erhsq37n]).

- Africa’s real capital challenge is not simply about access or scale, as is often framed in academic and policy debates; it is more of Africa’s inability to attract the right kind of capital.
- Investment structures that prioritize short-term returns from extraction are poorly aligned with the long-term financing needs and structure for a green mineral-led industrialization in Africa.

Africa can no longer rely on old investment models. It must think and do things differently: blend public, private, and development finance, design instruments that reward real and genuine local impact and build partnerships that go beyond extraction toward industrial transformation.

The question, therefore, is not whether Africa can attract capital—it is whether it can structure that capital to deliver transformation.

The ability of Africa’s green minerals to power its future industrial base, generate jobs, and support sustainable green growth ultimately depends on it.

Elvis K. Avenyo (Ph.D.) Solomon Owusu Woubet Kassa, PhD Emmanuel Buadi Mensah
